Content:
[MATH: T(x,y) = (x+4,y+2)]

Content:
The function above takes a point as its input and gives another point as output. Let's check it with our point [MATH: Q(1,2){:}]

Content:
[MATH: T(1, 2) = (1 + 4, 2 + 2) = (5, 4)✓]

Content:
Any translation of [MATH: a] units to the right and [MATH: b] units up can be written using any of the following notations:
[MATH: (x, y) ↦ (x + a, y + b); T(x, y) = (x + a, y + b)]

sections.normalized_html: The translation [MATH: (x,y) \mapsto(x+p, y+q)] maps the polygon [MATH: \mathcal{P}] to the polygon [MATH: \mathcal{Q}] as shown above. What are the values of [MATH: p] and [MATH: q?]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/dcb54a388fde5534e4b09f07e5c983f0]

The translation [MATH: (x,y) \mapsto(x+p, y+q)] maps the polygon [MATH: \mathcal{P}] to the polygon [MATH: \mathcal{Q}] as shown above. What are the values of [MATH: p] and [MATH: q?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Every point belonging to [MATH: \mathcal{P}] is translated in the same way. Therefore to determine the values of [MATH: p] and [MATH: q,] we can consider any point of the polygon.

Let's consider the vertex [MATH: (-2,2).] Under the translation, it moves to [MATH: (8,1).] So, we have

[MATH: (-2, 2) \mapsto (-2+p, 2+q)= (8,1).]

We establish the values of [MATH: p] and [MATH: q] by considering the [MATH: x]- and [MATH: y]-coordinates of the above transformation.

  • Looking at the [MATH: x]-coordinates, we must have [MATH: -2+p = 8,] so [MATH: p=10.]

  • Looking at the [MATH: y]-coordinates, we must have [MATH: 2+q=1,] so [MATH: q=-1.]

Therefore, [MATH: p=10] and [MATH: q=-1.]

- It's important to realize that every point on [MATH: \mathcal T] is translated to a point on [MATH: \mathcal T'.] The diagram shows the triangle's vertices being translated, but the same translation applies to every point on each side of the triangle as well.

Item 9 — Example: Solving for Missing Values in the Functional Representation of a Translation

The translation [MATH: (x,y) \mapsto(x+p, y+q)] maps the polygon [MATH: \mathcal{P}] to the polygon [MATH: \mathcal{Q}] as shown above. What are the values of [MATH: p] and [MATH: q?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Every point belonging to [MATH: \mathcal{P}] is translated in the same way. Therefore to determine the values of [MATH: p] and [MATH: q,] we can consider any point of the polygon.

Let's consider the vertex [MATH: (-2,2).] Under the translation, it moves to [MATH: (8,1).] So, we have

[MATH: (-2, 2) \mapsto (-2+p, 2+q)= (8,1).]

We establish the values of [MATH: p] and [MATH: q] by considering the [MATH: x]- and [MATH: y]-coordinates of the above transformation.

- Looking at the [MATH: x]-coordinates, we must have [MATH: -2+p = 8,] so [MATH: p=10.]
- Looking at the [MATH: y]-coordinates, we must have [MATH: 2+q=1,] so [MATH: q=-1.]

Therefore, [MATH: p=10] and [MATH: q=-1.]
